summary:
Mars Walk Planner is a tactical planetary navigation and EVA planning system created by Team Tech Slayers for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, tailored for human spacewalks across Mount Sharp in Gale Crater.

Core Capabilities
Suit-Aware A* Pathfinding: Evaluates a 1-meter hazard grid to route around impassable terrain (>18∘ slopes, sand traps, comms shadows) while continuously enforcing Safe-Return rings and Point-of-No-Return life-support margins.
Google Maps-Grade Navigation: Delivers real-time turn-by-turn maneuver HUD cards, cardinal bearings, landmark search autocomplete, an expandable directions drawer, and synthesized audio prompts.
Martian GPS & Constellation Positioning: Provides sub-2m positioning triangulated across 4 Mars relay orbiters (MRO, MAVEN, Odyssey, MEX) via Electra Prox-1 UHF, a Google Maps-style "My Location" FAB with geodetic accuracy circles, and hardware device GPS mapping 1:1 Earth footsteps to Mars.
Real NASA Planetary Data: Fuses USGS/NASA CTX, HiRISE, MOLA elevation, Curiosity Mastcam rover imagery, REMS weather, and MSL RAD radiation telemetry.
Resilient Architecture: Operates with a decoupled event bus, circuit breakers, token-bucket rate limiting, and compensation-backed emergency recovery sagas.
details: Mars Walk Planner is a web app that helps a Mars astronaut plan and carry out a single spacewalk at Mount Sharp, Gale Crater. It layers NASA and partner data on one local map: orbital imagery, elevation and slope, thermal inertia (sand-trap risk), mineral maps, radiation, and weather. The astronaut confirms three science waypoints (sulfate vein, boxwork ridge, carbonate hollow). A suit-aware A* pathfinding algorithm then finds the safest route between them. Each map cell gets a traversal cost from slope, sand-trap risk and radio line-of-sight, and slopes over 18° are treated as impassable. During the spacewalk, a live view tracks oxygen, battery, radiation, weather and return limit, shows rover photos near each waypoint, and warns when the astronaut reaches the point of no return. A “Simulate EVA Emergency” button demonstrates a dust gust, an automatic reroute and a safe return path.
